Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

risks_and_remaining_uncertainty: No builds/tests/probes were run by planner; this report is design, not acceptance or verification evidence. Source inspection and live task reads only.

Current protocol progress is crash-resume information, not an independent complete per-item ledger. Never reinterpret an advanced hash-bearing position as proof the culprit succeeded. Tests need explicit required-item completion fixtures for the fully recovered control.

## Original definition (verbatim)

4. **FOS-000004 — Retain unrecoverable child loss in the controller.** **S–M; no dependencies; §2–§4.** [Linux shutdown:335](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L335) and [Windows shutdown:278](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L278) use the same boolean for “do not restart because done” and “cannot continue.” Their callers restart conditionally but otherwise continue to exit success ([Linux:1429](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_linux.hpp#L1429), [Windows:1035](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay_windows.hpp#L1035)). Separate restart disposition from the retained worker outcome. Immediately return an aggregate unsuccessful result when assigned required work is unresolved. **Check:** E5/E6; clean worker; failed worker alongside a clean worker; failure before resource identity is known. Record the assigned range and unknown remainder. Do not fail all successfully recovered attempts just because a child once died.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Controller subprocess tests on Linux and Windows:** A worker lost before its first progress report produces an unsuccessful controller outcome, retaining its assigned range and unknown remainder. Repeat with another worker succeeding and with worker report order reversed; the unsuccessful aggregate is unchanged.
   - **Recovery control tests:** Clean completion succeeds; a failed attempt followed by verified completion of every required item can succeed. A skipped required culprit or unresolved range cannot succeed. Assert the controller result directly, independently of stderr and optional shared progress.

source_review: Entire base-to-candidate diff inspected, including common outcome state, Linux and Windows lifecycle/cleanup code, ExternalReplayer Linux status caching, CMake registration, controller and CLI test sources, and verification documentation.

Assigned half-open ranges initialize once and survive retry-start mutation. Known culprit index/hash is captured independently of optional shared progress. Absent or invalid required-kind progress prevents retry and retains unknown remainder; empty kinds require no fake progress.

All Linux harvest paths consume Unresolved; Windows normal-process and timer shutdown callers consume Unresolved. Early unsuccessful return invokes scoped child termination/reaping. Parent-requested cleanup is excluded from legacy crash counts.

Linux waitpid observation error is retained; Windows WaitForSingleObject/GetExitCodeProcess failure never defaults to code zero success and preserves native_error across handle closure/cleanup. Windows source/registration reviewed only; native execution waived/unverified.

Actual master loops, fork/CreateProcess, pipes, waits, shutdown parsing and restart state remain in the test executable. Test-only adapters alter worker behavior and terminal harvesting, not outcome aggregation. Explicit DiagnosticChecks survive NDEBUG.

Mixed-order fixtures barrier both children at terminal state before deterministic harvest selection and require successful sibling marker. Held-sibling fixture waits on IPC and asserts kernel termination/reaping. Recovery fixture checks exact retry range and every required item marker.
Graphics, compute and ray-tracing culprit fixtures cover beginning/last required item; clean tail cannot erase failure. Partial-progress and loss-after-retry retain original range and known prefix.

Public ExternalReplayer declarations and SharedControlBlock layout/version unchanged. Existing protocol literals and index/hash semantics exercised. Intentional behavior change is unsuccessful robust-controller exit propagating to caller; no general binary ABI claim.

Release historical malformed fixture follows a parse rejection without worker death. Preserving its zero exit is an out-of-scope parser-policy limitation; counters must show parsefail1/skip1/complete0/deaths0 and deterministic worker loss must exit1 in every configuration.
Zero selected ranges use populated FOZ; empty-archive additionally reads back zero resources for every tag. Both use production master and explicit result/state assertions.
